static_traits.name: Li Ruian
static_traits.family_status: Lives alone, keeps a koi fish named 'Spot'
static_traits.social_status: Has one close friend to confide in, but has not yet discussed gardening-related anxiety with them; social participation is limited due to excessive focus on garden outcomes
static_traits.medical_history: No history of similar psychological problems; has not received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Neutral attitude; clear and organized expression; able to describe problems and triggering situations concretely; good cooperation; has cognitive tendencies toward catastrophizing and fortune telling

basic_info.main_problem: Persistent anxiety and stress about gardening yields (especially tomatoes); it intensified a few months ago when I noticed the tomatoes growing slower than usual; every time I check on or think about the garden I worry the whole season's harvest will fail.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent anxiety and stress have left me overwhelmed, and I am seeking counseling for support and guidance.
growth_experiences: A few months ago, he noticed the tomatoes were growing more slowly than usual, and anxiety and stress arose and gradually intensified; every time he checks or thinks about the garden, he worries that the whole season's harvest will fail. He tried self-comfort and searching online for gardening advice, but this did not help, and it went on to affect work focus, social participation, sleep, and appetite.

core_beliefs: If the harvest fails, I will be very embarrassed, and all the time and energy spent before will be wasted

special_situations.event: Several months ago, noticing that tomatoes were growing more slowly than usual
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If growth progress is abnormal, it means it will ultimately fail
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Searching extensively online for gardening advice and repeatedly checking the plants
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The entire season's harvest will fail

special_situations.event: Every time checking the garden or thinking about the plants
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not immediately handle every problem, the harvest will fail
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly monitoring, frequently checking and researching in an attempt to control the outcome
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I do not keep watching them, they will die

special_situations.event: Noticing a few yellow leaves on a plant
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Any negative sign means the whole crop will fail
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Researching online for a long time and checking again and again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The entire crop may be doomed to fail

special_situations.event: Distracted at work, thinking about the state of the garden
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the harvest fails, all investment becomes waste and is embarrassing
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to comfort oneself and seeking advice online
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I fail this time, my efforts will have no meaning at all

core_conflict.wish: Longing to obtain a successful harvest and a stable sense of control through effort
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure, disappointment and shame (feeling investment will be negated)
defense_goal: Reduces uncertainty and failure risk through continuous monitoring and intellectualization (extensively looking up information)

object_relations.self_representation: A self that works hard but worries about failure
object_relations.object_representation: An unpredictable garden/tomato plants that may have problems at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When plant abnormalities are observed (such as yellow leaves) or when asked to describe specific worries
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tends to interpret small changes or counseling inquiries as signals that 'the harvest will fail', believing a solution must be found immediately or things will get out of control
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Adopts a fact-oriented, gentle and neutral tone, focusing on evidence and feasible steps, avoiding emotional expression.

manifestations: Worrying that failure will turn the invested time and energy into waste
Persistent worry about the outcome because the tomatoes are growing slowly
Anxiety appears whenever thinking of the garden

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for them, and instead does it to the self, turning the energy originally meant to be sent outward toward the self.
manifestations: Not having discussed gardening-related anxiety with close friends
Turns anxious energy toward the self: spends long periods online looking up information and repeatedly checks the plants

exception_events.target_problem: When noticing plant abnormalities or checking the garden, the client usually experiences persistent anxiety, repeatedly searches online for information and checks frequently, resulting in worsened anxiety and difficulty focusing on work and socializing.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once, the client only watered the plants and temporarily stopped paying excessive attention; for a few days they did not check frequently and felt more relaxed.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: telling themselves 'give the plants some space, they need time', reducing monitoring and online searching, so this time brief relief and relaxation occurred.

positive_force: Able to notice and self-soothe (such as reminding oneself that plants need time)
Willing to explore and accept decatastrophizing training and strategies
Having a relatively stable occupational functioning foundation (work only mildly disturbed)
Having a friend who can provide emotional support (though not yet used)
negative_force: Catastrophizing and fortune-telling cognitive patterns (worrying the whole season's harvest will fail)
Strong fear of failure and shame, tending to interpret the value of investment in an all-or-nothing way
Excessive monitoring and repeated information-seeking maintain anxiety
Disturbed sleep and appetite, social participation and work focus affected
not yet actively seeking social support

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent anxiety and excessive monitoring around tomato growing (repeatedly checking references and frequent inspections)
antecedent: Noticed tomatoes growing more slowly than usual
Every time checking the garden or thinking about the plants
Seeing negative signs such as yellow leaves
Distracted at work by thoughts of the garden
target_behavior.core_reason: Driven by catastrophic cognitions about harvest failure and the belief that 'failure means waste/shame', attempts to eliminate uncertainty through control
target_behavior.function: Avoids uncertainty and potential failure, gaining a temporary sense of control and security
target_behavior.consequence: Anxiety worsened, affecting work performance and social participation; sleep and appetite disturbed
